jobDescription: An industrial automation company supplies autonomous mobile robots, and the fleet software that coordinates them, to customer warehouses. The fleet software team writes the traffic-management and task-allocation services in C++ and Python, simulates layouts before a site changes its floor plan and supports site engineers when robots stall. The engineer will improve task allocation, extend the simulator, write field diagnostics and follow the company's safety-related software process. Idle-time and throughput improvements are reported from fleet telemetry for named sites and dated periods.
requirements: Develops fleet traffic-management or task-allocation services in C++ or Python.
Extends a layout simulator used to test fleet behaviour before site changes.
Shows a measured improvement in robot idle time or throughput from fleet telemetry against a baseline period.
Writes field diagnostics and supports site engineers during robot stalls.
Works within a safety-related software process such as IEC 61508 or ISO 13849, including writing safety requirements.

evidence.text: Rewrote the task-allocation service in C++ at Brannock Automation so that robots are assigned picks by estimated travel time rather than straight-line distance.
Added one-way aisle rules and charger queues to the Python layout simulator, and ran each customer's proposed layout through it before the site engineers changed the floor plan.

At the Daventry and Leeds customer sites, robot idle time went from 14.0% of shift time in the baseline fortnight (6 to 19 February 2023) to 9.6% after the new allocation went into service (20 March to 2 April 2023), measured from fleet telemetry.
Wrote a field diagnostics command that dumps a stalled robot's path plan and sensor state, and joined the weekday support rota for site engineers.
Followed the company's safety-related software process for the allocation service: hazard-log entries, code review by a second engineer and test reports filed for the safety case.

Work sample: the telemetry comparison report for the two sites, with idle-time tables for the baseline and post-change fortnights (14.0% and 9.6% of shift time), the fleet manager's definition of idle time, the allocation release date (13 March 2023) and acknowledgements from both site operations managers.
HR verification note: employment at Brannock Automation from January 2021 to May 2024 with the job title Software Engineer was confirmed through the background-screening provider's employer contact.

Reference check summary: the former fleet software manager confirmed in writing that the candidate wrote the travel-time allocation change and that it was released to the Daventry and Leeds sites in March 2023.

propositions.text: Robot idle time at the Daventry and Leeds sites went from 14.0% of shift time (6 to 19 February 2023) to 9.6% (20 March to 2 April 2023) after the candidate's task-allocation change went into service, measured from fleet telemetry.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the figures and periods, the work sample carries the telemetry tables and definition, and the reference check confirms the candidate wrote the released change.

propositions.text: The candidate rewrote the task-allocation service in C++ to assign picks by estimated travel time.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the rewrite and the reference check confirms it in writing.

propositions.text: The candidate added one-way aisle rules and charger queues to the Python layout simulator.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the simulator work directly.

gold.expectedGap: The candidate followed the internal safety process, but the standard it maps to and any writing of safety requirements are not described.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the idle-time result with its two sites, fortnight windows and telemetry definition; do not extend it to other sites or to throughput, which the sources do not report.
followUpTargets: Ask which functional-safety standard the company's process followed and whether the candidate wrote any safety requirements.
